Halogens (X: F, Cl, Br & I) form binary compounds with hydrogen commonly known as
hydrogen halides (or haloacids). Their aqueous solution is called hydrohalic acids.
HCl(g) + H2O → HCl (aq)
(Hydrogen chloride)

Let us discuss some of the methods of preparation haloacids (HX: HCl, HBr & HI)
1. By the action of conc. sulphuric acid on metal halides (Laboratory preparation) In laboratory HCl gas is prepared by heating common salt with conc. sulphuric acid.
NaCl + conc. H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HCl (at low temperature)

NaCl + conc. H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + HCl (at high temperature) 2NaCl + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2HCl This method cannot be applied to prepare HBr and HI. This is because both HBr and HI are powerful reducing agents. Therefore, HBr and HI produced quickly reduce sulphuric acid to sulphur dioxide and themselves get oxidized to Br2 and I2 respectively. NaBr + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HBr}×2 H2SO4 → H2O + SO2 + [O] 2HBr + [O] → H2O + Br2 2NaBr + 3H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + SO2 + Br2 + 2H2O Similarly,
KI + H2SO4 → KHSO4 + HI}×2 H2SO4 → H2O + SO2 + [O]

2HI + [O] → H2O + I2 2KI + 3H2SO4 → 2KHSO4 + SO2 + I2 + 2H2O Hence, HBr and HI are prepared by heating bromide and iodide salt with non-oxidizing agents like phosphoric acid. NaBr + H3PO4 → NaH2PO4 + HBr NaI + H3PO4 → NaH2PO4 + HI Test yourself!

HF has abnormally high b.p. due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding between their molecules. 9.4.5 Comparative chemical properties of HX (HCl, HBr and HI):
Some of the chemical properties of hydrogen halides are listed below:

1. Reducing nature Hydrogen halides behave as a reducing agent. Their reducing power decreases in the order, HI˃ HBr˃ HCl ˃HF. This is because on moving from F to I in the group bond dissociation energy of H-X decreases and reducing strength increases. Some examples that show reducing nature of haloacids are:

HCl reduces MnO2, KMnO4, K2Cr2O7 etc. MnO2 + 2HCl → MnCl2 + H2O + [O] 2HCl + [O] → H2O + Cl2 MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + Cl2 + H2O 2KMnO4 → K2O + 2MnO + 5[O] K2O + 2HCl → 2KCl + H2O {MnO + 2HCl → MnCl2 + H2O}×2 {2HCl + [O] → Cl2 + H2O}×5 2KMnO4+ 16HCl → 2KCl + 2MnCl2 + 5Cl2 + 8H2O HBr and HI react in the similar manner as HCl does. HI can even reduce ferric salt to ferrous salt, sulphuric acid to sulphur dioxide, nitric acid to nitrogen dioxide, etc.
